title: The Standing Deposit Allowance Taken Off a Raised Auto Loans Rate
content:
An allowance is taken off the raised rate when the rate on a loan of the Auto Loans line is restated. Its size turns on two readings of the borrower's Personal Checking account: whether they hold an active checking account whose posted balance is at least the fee-waiver daily balance its tier publishes, and whether at least 2 recurring deposits have posted to that account in the last three months.

| How many of the two readings hold | Standing deposit allowance |
|---|---|
| Both | 1.2 percent of the raised rate |
| Exactly one | 0.6 percent of the raised rate |
| Neither | 0.00 |

The standing deposit allowance is 1.2 percent of the raised rate where both of these hold, that the borrower holds an active checking account whose posted balance is at least the fee-waiver daily balance its tier publishes and that at least 2 recurring deposits have posted to that account in the last three months. It is 0.6 percent of the raised rate where exactly one of those two holds. It is 0.00 where neither of them holds.

## The allowance is a share, not a fixed number of points

Both of the first two rows read as a percentage of the raised rate, so the allowance grows with the rate it is taken off. On a raised rate of 8.84, the top row gives an allowance of 0.10608 and the middle row gives 0.05304. On a raised rate of 5.00, the same rows give 0.06 and 0.03.

## How the two readings are taken

The balance reading compares the posted balance on the borrower's active account in the Personal Checking line against the fee-waiver daily balance published for that account's tier, so the comparison figure moves with the tier held. The deposit reading counts recurring deposits posted to that same account over the three months ending on the day of the restatement; exactly 2 meets the reading and 1 does not.
